{
  "IP": "neorv32_xbus",
  "Conceptual Assets": [
    {
      "Concept ID": "C1",
      "Concept Name": "External bus access address",
      "Unit": "neorv32_xbus",
      "Information": "The target address of each external bus access determines which external resource is selected. It enters with the bus request and is forwarded to the external address output.",
      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "yes",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "no",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "no"
      },
      "Rubric Reason": "The address can expose access patterns at xbus_adr_o on line 141. Altering the forwarded address path at lines 74 and 141 can route an access to an unintended target.",
      "Objectives At Risk": [
        "C",
        "I"
      ],
      "Attack": "An attacker could monitor xbus_adr_o to infer protected accesses or alter the address so a read or write reaches the wrong external resource.",
      "Enters Through": [
        "bus_req_i.addr"
      ],
      "Leaves Through": [
        "xbus_adr_o"
      ],
      "Entry Lines": [
        72
      ],
      "Held Lines": [
        141
      ],
      "Exit Lines": [
        141
      ]
    },
    {
      "Concept ID": "C2",
      "Concept Name": "External bus transfer direction",
      "Unit": "neorv32_xbus",
      "Information": "The read/write direction of an external bus transfer determines whether the selected resource is read or modified. It is forwarded from the request to xbus_we_o.",
      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "no",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "no",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "no"
      },
      "Rubric Reason": "Changing the forwarded direction at lines 74 and 143 can turn a read into a write or a write into a read.",
      "Objectives At Risk": [
        "I"
      ],
      "Attack": "An attacker could alter the direction bit so a transaction writes when it should read or reads when it should write.",
      "Enters Through": [
        "bus_req_i.rw"
      ],
      "Leaves Through": [
        "xbus_we_o"
      ],
      "Entry Lines": [
        72
      ],
      "Held Lines": [
        143
      ],
      "Exit Lines": [
        143
      ]
    },
    {
      "Concept ID": "C3",
      "Concept Name": "Debug request marker",
      "Unit": "neorv32_xbus",
      "Information": "The debug request marker identifies an external bus transaction as a debug transaction and is encoded into the xbus tag. External behavior can depend on this marker.",
      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "no",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "no",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "yes"
      },
      "Rubric Reason": "Changing bus_req_i.debug before it is combined into xbus_tag_o at line 151 can cause an external transaction to be treated as a debug transaction. An injected or altered debug marker can make the normal access behavior incorrect through the path at lines 72 and 151.",
      "Objectives At Risk": [
        "I"
      ],
      "Attack": "An attacker could inject or suppress the debug marker so an external target grants debug treatment to a normal transaction or rejects a legitimate one.",
      "Enters Through": [
        "bus_req_i.debug"
      ],
      "Leaves Through": [
        "xbus_tag_o"
      ],
      "Entry Lines": [
        72
      ],
      "Held Lines": [
        151
      ],
      "Exit Lines": [
        151
      ]
    },
    {
      "Concept ID": "C4",
      "Concept Name": "Privilege-mode marker",
      "Unit": "neorv32_xbus",
      "Information": "The privilege-mode marker identifies the privilege context of an external bus transaction and is encoded into xbus_tag_o. External access authorization can depend on this marker.",
      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "no",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "no",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "no"
      },
      "Rubric Reason": "Changing bus_req_i.priv before the tag assignment at line 151 can cause the external target to interpret the transaction as having a different privilege level.",
      "Objectives At Risk": [
        "I"
      ],
      "Attack": "An attacker could alter the privilege marker so an external target authorizes an access that should be restricted or rejects an access that should be allowed.",
      "Enters Through": [
        "bus_req_i.priv"
      ],
      "Leaves Through": [
        "xbus_tag_o"
      ],
      "Entry Lines": [
        72
      ],
      "Held Lines": [
        151
      ],
      "Exit Lines": [
        151
      ]
    },
    {
      "Concept ID": "C5",
      "Concept Name": "In-flight bus transfer state",
      "Unit": "neorv32_xbus",
      "Information": "The pending state records that a bus request is being served and controls how long the external cycle and response remain active. The state depends on the request strobe and completion or fault conditions.",
      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "no",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "yes",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "no"
      },
      "Rubric Reason": "Unauthorized modification of pending at lines 85, 89, 93, and 97 can cause a transfer to be reported or terminated incorrectly. Pending directly controls xbus_cyc_o at line 146 and response generation at lines 154 through 156, so corrupting it can withhold or block a required transfer.",
      "Objectives At Risk": [
        "I",
        "A"
      ],
      "Attack": "An attacker could clear pending before completion to lose a transfer or hold it active so the bus remains blocked.",
      "Enters Through": [
        "bus_req_i.stb"
      ],
      "Leaves Through": [
        "xbus_cyc_o",
        "bus_rsp_o.ack",
        "bus_rsp_o.err"
      ],
      "Entry Lines": [
        72
      ],
      "Held Lines": [
        85,
        89,
        93,
        97
      ],
      "Exit Lines": [
        73,
        146
      ]
    },
    {
      "Concept ID": "C6",
      "Concept Name": "External transfer completion acknowledgment",
      "Unit": "neorv32_xbus",
      "Information": "The completion acknowledgment indicates that an outstanding external transfer has completed and is returned in the bus response. It is derived from xbus_ack_i together with the active-transfer state.",
      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "no",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "yes",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "no"
      },
      "Rubric Reason": "The acknowledgment is produced from xbus_ack_i at line 155 and returned through bus_rsp_o at lines 75 and 73, so it can be falsified to complete a transfer early or suppressed to prevent completion.       "Objectives At Risk": [
        "I",
        "A"
      ],
      "Attack": "An attacker could forge xbus_ack_i to complete an unfinished access or suppress it so the requester waits indefinitely.",
      "Enters Through": [
        "xbus_ack_i"
      ],
      "Leaves Through": [
        "bus_rsp_o.ack"
      ],
      "Entry Lines": [
        155
      ],
      "Held Lines": [
        155
      ],
      "Exit Lines": [
        73,
        75
      ]
    },
    {
      "Concept ID": "C7",
      "Concept Name": "External bus fault status",
      "Unit": "neorv32_xbus",
      "Information": "The external fault indication reports that the target bus signaled an error and contributes to completion and error reporting. It enters through xbus_err_i and leaves in the bus response.",
      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "no",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "no",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "no"
      },
      "Rubric Reason": "Changing xbus_err_i changes bus_rsp.err and bus_rsp.ack at lines 155 and 156 and can also terminate pending at line 92, producing an incorrect fault result or prematurely aborting an access.",
      "Objectives At Risk": [
        "I"
      ],
      "Attack": "An attacker could assert or suppress xbus_err_i to make a valid access fail, conceal a target fault, or terminate the transfer with a false error.",
      "Enters Through": [
        "xbus_err_i"
      ],
      "Leaves Through": [
        "bus_rsp_o.err",
        "bus_rsp_o.ack"
      ],
      "Entry Lines": [
        155,
        156
      ],
      "Held Lines": [
        156
      ],
      "Exit Lines": [
        73,
        75
      ]
    },
    {
      "Concept ID": "C8",
      "Concept Name": "Bus timeout protection state",
      "Unit": "neorv32_xbus",
      "Information": "The internal timeout counter and timeout indication bound how long an outstanding transfer may wait and generate a completion/error when the deadline expires. It has no entry port because its deadline is fixed by the build-time generic and its counter is generated internally.",
      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "no",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "yes",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "no"
      },
      "Rubric Reason": "Changing the counter or timeout indication at lines 112 through 122 can abort a valid transfer or alter its reported result. Suppressing the timeout can leave pending active indefinitely, while asserting it can terminate a required transfer, affecting lines 92, 96, 155, and 156.",
      "Objectives At Risk": [
        "I",
        "A"
      ],
      "Attack": "An attacker could manipulate the timeout state to force premature bus errors or suppress expiration so a stalled transfer blocks the bus.",
      "Enters Through": [],
      "Leaves Through": [
        "bus_rsp_o.ack",
        "bus_rsp_o.err"
      ],
      "Entry Lines": [],
      "Held Lines": [
        112,
        113,
        116,
        117,
        120,
        122,
        131,
        132
      ],
      "Exit Lines": [
        73,
        155,
        156
      ]
    }
  ],
  "Not Kept": [
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Relayed bus payload and response data",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_xbus",
      "Merged Into": "",
      "Why Not Kept": "The request and response data only move between bus ports and the external bus without being stored or computed by this unit, so the forwarded-transaction and relayed-data rules bar them as pieces of their own."
    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Other forwarded transaction fields",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_xbus",
      "Merged Into": "",
      "Why Not Kept": "AMO fields, byte enables, fence, and source metadata are only forwarded or used as external transaction metadata and are not independently stored, computed, or checked by this unit."
    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Lock bookkeeping copy",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_xbus",
      "Merged Into": "",
      "Why Not Kept": "The locked register only copies the access lock bit and is read to end or retain the access in progress, so the bus-handshake-copy rule bars it as an independent piece."
    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Timeout counter",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_xbus",
      "Merged Into": "C8",
      "Why Not Kept": ""
    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Clock and reset control",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_xbus",
      "Merged Into": "",
      "Why Not Kept": "clk_i and rstn_i only time or reset the unit and its register-stage instance, and the explicit clock/reset rule excludes them as conceptual assets."
    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "TIMEOUT_VAL build-time configuration",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_xbus",
      "Merged Into": "",
      "Why Not Kept": "TIMEOUT_VAL is a generic that fixes the build and cannot be changed or withheld by an element of the IP at run time."
    }
  ],
  "Notes": []
}

conceptual assets.information: The target address of each external bus access determines which external resource is selected. It enters with the bus request and is forwarded to the external address output.

conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could monitor xbus_adr_o to infer protected accesses or alter the address so a read or write reaches the wrong external resource.

conceptual assets.information: The read/write direction of an external bus transfer determines whether the selected resource is read or modified. It is forwarded from the request to xbus_we_o.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Changing the forwarded direction at lines 74 and 143 can turn a read into a write or a write into a read.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could alter the direction bit so a transaction writes when it should read or reads when it should write.

conceptual assets.information: The debug request marker identifies an external bus transaction as a debug transaction and is encoded into the xbus tag. External behavior can depend on this marker.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Changing bus_req_i.debug before it is combined into xbus_tag_o at line 151 can cause an external transaction to be treated as a debug transaction. An injected or altered debug marker can make the normal access behavior incorrect through the path at lines 72 and 151.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could inject or suppress the debug marker so an external target grants debug treatment to a normal transaction or rejects a legitimate one.

conceptual assets.information: The privilege-mode marker identifies the privilege context of an external bus transaction and is encoded into xbus_tag_o. External access authorization can depend on this marker.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Changing bus_req_i.priv before the tag assignment at line 151 can cause the external target to interpret the transaction as having a different privilege level.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could alter the privilege marker so an external target authorizes an access that should be restricted or rejects an access that should be allowed.

conceptual assets.information: The pending state records that a bus request is being served and controls how long the external cycle and response remain active. The state depends on the request strobe and completion or fault conditions.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Unauthorized modification of pending at lines 85, 89, 93, and 97 can cause a transfer to be reported or terminated incorrectly. Pending directly controls xbus_cyc_o at line 146 and response generation at lines 154 through 156, so corrupting it can withhold or block a required transfer.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could clear pending before completion to lose a transfer or hold it active so the bus remains blocked.

conceptual assets.information: The completion acknowledgment indicates that an outstanding external transfer has completed and is returned in the bus response. It is derived from xbus_ack_i together with the active-transfer state.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The acknowledgment is produced from xbus_ack_i at line 155 and returned through bus_rsp_o at lines 75 and 73, so it can be falsified to complete a transfer early or suppressed to prevent completion. Suppressing or fabricating completion can stall the requester or lose the required transfer response.

considered, not kept.reason: The request and response data only move between bus ports and the external bus without being stored or computed by this unit, so the forwarded-transaction and relayed-data rules bar them as pieces of their own.
AMO fields, byte enables, fence, and source metadata are only forwarded or used as external transaction metadata and are not independently stored, computed, or checked by this unit.
The locked register only copies the access lock bit and is read to end or retain the access in progress, so the bus-handshake-copy rule bars it as an independent piece.
clk_i and rstn_i only time or reset the unit and its register-stage instance, and the explicit clock/reset rule excludes them as conceptual assets.
